reason: The passage emphasizes hierarchy through multiple structural elements: (1) God's explicit commands to establish a chain of authority through anointing - Elijah is commanded to anoint Hazael as king over Aram (חזאל לְמֶלֶךְ), Jehu as king over Israel (יְהוּא לְמֶלֶךְ), and Elisha as prophet successor (לְנָבִיא תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ - 'prophet in your place'); (2) The principle of ordained succession, where authority is formally transferred from one person to the next through divine appointment; (3) The hierarchical chain itself: God commands Elijah, who will anoint kings and a prophet, establishing religious and political authority structures. The anointing formula emphasizes that these positions are divinely ordained rather than self-assumed, reinforcing the legitimacy of hierarchical authority.
